title: Scope and Local Variables in Functions
learningObjectives: Explain scope and local variables in functions.
Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: Local variables belong to their declared block or function scope. Each ordinary call creates its own local variables. A static local persists across calls. Variables must be initialized before their values are read.
understand.whyItMatters: Local state limits coupling and prevents accidental interference between unrelated parts of a program.
understand.explain: A local name is unavailable outside its scope. Returning a reference or pointer to a local is unsafe because the local's lifetime ends on return. Keep temporary variables narrowly scoped and initialize them explicitly.

examples.code: int first(){int count=1;return count;}\nint second(){int count=2;return count;}

examples.title: Narrow block scope
examples.code: int total=0;{int bonus=3;total+=bonus;}\n// bonus is out of scope here
examples.explanation: A block limits the lifetime and visibility of bonus.

examples.title: Static local persists
examples.explanation: The static local retains its value across calls; use this state intentionally.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Scope and Local Variables in Functions examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Write two functions with independent local variables using the same names. Add a helper with a static call counter and trace its output across repeated calls. Explain lifetime differences.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.
